findings: ChangeFrontlineLimiter now only emits its three-field notification and queues captured integer/remove parameters; it does not mutate the limiter collection during production.

Limiter and existing Gotcha play receipts share a FIFO queue. Collection add/remove happens only while consuming the local receipt batch, without re-emitting notifications or looking up a limiter object.

Existing known finish sites (play/move/attack/start/end turn and selection completion) consume the shared queue. Old Gotcha-only public method forwards for compatibility. No outer-effect-end blanket drain was introduced.

Existing24scenario/96call parameter contract now verifies production vs consumption;96dynamic batch cases now retain initial capacity throughout construction/entry and only update the collection at receipt.

New48case integration matrix covers both sides, normal play, hand-target reply, draw-selection reply, initial limiter on/off, and add/remove/add-then-remove/remove-then-add. Nested batch admission uses initial capacity, Gotcha remains deferred, final receipts apply once.
New4case deferred-hand-reply matrix verifies initial action receipt before answering, inverse update remains unapplied during reply/AfterWait, and reply completion consumes it.
Mutable synthetic IR fixtures evict and restore only their own local cache entry, preventing prior probe programs from contaminating the new matrix.

tests.before: 3/555 failed with deferred expectations and old kernel

limits: This repairs the evidenced limiter production/application difference at existing normal action and reply finish sites, not complete PvP action scheduling.
Only limiter and Gotcha receipts are modeled here; other local/remote subaction handlers, marker insertion, reconnect/validation/error paths and native receive reentry remain unaudited.
PlayerMoves.DoNextInQueue per-card standalone autoplay path is still separate and not fully modeled. This change does not certify it or add a universal receipt boundary.
Headless dispatch still assumes the gameplay/IsActionProcess=true path; native false-path no-op behavior and full flag lifecycle are not restored.
Direct standalone API callers must explicitly finish a local receipt batch. ActionLog still represents emitted subactions as separate GameActions rather than native grouped action packets.

Tests use controlled synthetic programs/callbacks and captured static definitions. They do not certify each real card, full native timing, exceptions, GC/TSet iteration, or deeper nested receive behavior.
No historical replay authority, live process writes/injection or new game memory capture. Fully semantically verified cards remains0.
